newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close with pared losses.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close with pared losses.

text.p: Thai stocks closed with pared losses on Thursday as bargain hunters moved in late to buy some finance issues, brokers said.
The SET index finished down 1.68 points to 712.61 on thin 2.2 billion baht turnover well above the day's low of 706.61. The SET-50 index shed 0.13 point to 53.09.
"Investors sold on disappointment at some key economic data released by the central bank earlier today," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
Decliners led gainers 170 to 128 while 91 issues remained unchanged.
Brokers said market sentiment was poor and investors were discouraged to enter the market after the Bank of Thailand released its monthly economic indicators, some of them were viewed as poor.
"Investors thought the country's balance of trade and balance of payments did not improve much," said Somchai.
The Bank of Thailand said the trade deficit in January widened to a preliminary 39.0 billion baht from 22.3 billion in December.
The central bank said the balance of payments position in February turned into a deficit of 26.6 billion baht from a surplus of 24.7 billion baht in January.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 120 baht while Siam Cement advanced eight to 636.
Among finance counters, Phatra Thanakit gained one to 43, Dhana Siam Finance rose 0.50 to 37 and Asia Credit gained two to end at 105.
Support is seen by some brokers at around 715 and resistance at 700 on Friday.
